Here $T$ is in kelvins, $p$ is in pascals, $m$ is total amount in moles, and $C^1$ means continuous first coordinate derivatives as in [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The chart dimension is $C+2$, matching the ambient dimension of $D_c$. The map $\sigma_\alpha$ takes values in numerical state coordinates; its physical SI state map is explicitly $\chi_\alpha=\Phi_c\circ\sigma_\alpha$, where $\Phi_c$ is the numerical-to-SI unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Thus the physical amounts at this point are $n_j=m x_j$, and the numerical amount coordinates in $\sigma_\alpha$ are $n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. Derivative-defined physical state functions are evaluated on $\chi_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$, or equivalently pulled back along $\Phi_c$ to $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$. At $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$ in this precise pullback sense, the derivative-defined state functions of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]] give temperature $T$, pressure $p$, and mole fractions $x_j=n_j/m$; here $n_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^C n_i=m$ uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]]. An **intensive phase branch** additionally has each derivative-defined chemical potential $\mu_j(T,p,x,m)$ independent of $m$ throughout $W_\alpha$; write its value as $\mu_j^\alpha(T,p,x)$. This scale invariance is an explicit constitutive model property, not a consequence of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A valid local response chart and its inverse are as in [[def-td-response-functions]] and [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Existence of $W_\alpha$ or $\sigma_\alpha$ is a model premise, not a consequence of the equations of thermodynamics.

On a branch with a valid natural-variable chart, $G^\alpha$ denotes the Gibbs potential of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]] restricted to the branch. For a one-component branch with amount $m_\alpha>0$, define $g_\alpha:=G^\alpha/m_\alpha$, $s_\alpha:=S_\alpha/m_\alpha$, and $v_\alpha:=V_\alpha/m_\alpha$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. This is the periodic retained-admissibility convention; it is not an unrestricted zero-beta limit of a shell law.

Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$, use the Euclidean norm $|\cdot|_2$ from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], define $|x|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$, and use the numerical coordinate conventions in [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. A finite configuration is a finite subset $\omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ with no repeated points; its number of points is $N(\omega)$. A pair potential is an even Borel function, measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra generated by open sets ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where even means $\phi(-x)=\phi(x)$. Define
$$H_\phi(\omega)=\sum_{\{x,y\}\subset\omega}\phi(x-y),\qquad H_\phi(\varnothing)=0.$$
The sum is over unordered two-point subsets, so every term is evaluated at a nonzero separation; if any term is $+\infty$, the sum is $+\infty$.

For $L>0$ put $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $V_L=L^d$, and let $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}$ be $H_\phi$ for configurations restricted to $\Lambda_L$. For sufficiently large periodic cubes, periodize $\omega\subset\Lambda_L$ by $\omega^{\mathrm{per}}=\{x+Lk:x\in\omega,\ k\in\mathbb Z^d\}$ and set
$$H_{L,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)=\frac12\sum_{x\in\omega}\sum_{y\in\omega^{\mathrm{per}},\ y\ne x}\phi(y-x),$$
interpreting the value as $+\infty$ if a positive infinite term occurs. The far image sum is absolutely convergent for all sufficiently large $L$ by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]; this is the image convention used below. With fixed numerical length and energy units, the canonical positional partition is
$$Z(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\Lambda_L^N}e^{-\beta H_\phi(q_1,\ldots,q_N)}dq_1\cdots dq_N,\quad Z(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
where $\beta>0$, and the grand partition is $\Xi(L;a,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}a^NZ(L,N;\beta)$ for numerical activity $a>0$. The normalized unit-intensity Poisson version is $Z_Q(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,\mathrm{free}}}]$; since the Poisson density contributes $e^{-V_L}$, $\Xi(L;z,\beta)=e^{V_L}Z_Q(L;z,\beta)$. A physical pressure identification is not part of this mathematical definition.

For a stationary probability law $P$ on the configuration space of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], write $\rho(P)=E_PN_{[0,1)^d}$. When the limit exists, write
$$\mathcal E(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}E_PH_{L,\mathrm{free}},\qquad I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}V_L^{-1}D(P_{\Lambda_L}\Vert Q_{\Lambda_L}).$$
The cited results below establish existence under their stated hypotheses; this definition does not assume it for every stationary law.

$$
\mathcal U_i(\lambda s,\lambda V,\lambda n)=\lambda\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)
$$
for all $\lambda$ in a neighborhood of $1$ for which the scaled state remains in the chart. This is a phase-branch hypothesis: the general tagged law of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] does not imply it. It may be stipulated independently on each local branch, or supplied by the common-law bulk subclass of [[pthm-td-euler-and-gibbs-duhem]] when each phase's local inverse states lie in its designated entropy cone with fixed species and intensive parameters and common SI units and energy/entropy reference conventions. Suppose a state $(T_0,p_0)\in O$ is an attained interior coexistence equilibrium with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange between the two branches, and both branches admit the valid local Gibbs charts of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Write $g_i=G_i/n_i$, $s_i=S_i/n_i$, and $v_i=V_i/n_i$ in the units specified by [[def-td-si-quantities]]. If
$$
\Delta v(T_0,p_0):=v_\beta(T_0,p_0)-v_\alpha(T_0,p_0)\ne0,
$$
then, on some open interval about $T_0$, the equal-Gibbs-per-mole coexistence condition $g_\alpha(T,p(T))=g_\beta(T,p(T))$ defines a unique local $C^1$ curve and
$$
\frac{dp}{dT}=\frac{s_\beta-s_\alpha}{v_\beta-v_\alpha}.
$$
If, in addition, conversion from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ is admitted as a reversible process in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at the same fixed $T$, and the full finite isolated compound (converted phases, reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries) has equilibrium endpoints with additive component entropy, with every component other than the converted phases and that reservoir having zero entropy change, then its molar latent heat absorbed by the system is $\ell_{\alpha\to\beta}=T(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. Assume a superstable regular pair potential $\phi$ as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and the van Hove definition [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]]. For a bounded Lebesgue-measurable $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, define $\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)=\{(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\Lambda^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ and $H_N(q)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)$. With $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, set
$$Z_\Lambda(N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)}e^{-\beta H_N(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_\Lambda(0;\beta)=1,\qquad \Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_\Lambda(N;\beta).$$
This is the labelled positional Lebesgue integral with indistinguishable-particle normalization and includes no exterior interaction. For $\Lambda=[0,L)^d$ it agrees with $Z(L,N;\beta)$ and $\Xi(L;z,\beta)$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For every van Hove sequence $(\Omega_k)$ and fixed $z,\beta>0$, the free-wall grand pressure satisfies
$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac1{|\Omega_k|}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)=p(z,\beta),$$
where $p(z,\beta)$ is the free-cube limit from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The extra superstability hypothesis supplies the uniform cell-occupation bound used below; no arbitrary-shape theorem under stability alone is claimed.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]: the stability constant $B$ gives $\phi(x)\geq-2B$ for nonzero separations, and regularity supplies $R_0<\infty$ and a nonnegative nonincreasing $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $|\phi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|_\infty)$ for $|x|_\infty\geq R_0$ and finite weighted tail integral.
[F3] [[lem-tdmath-superstable-cell-energy-bound]]: the energy dominates a positive cell-square sum minus a linear count.

1.1 Use the half-open unit-cell partition $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$ from [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]] and first take a finite union $\mathcal R$ of these cells. Let $\Pi_{\mathcal R}$ be the unnormalized positional sector measure whose $N$-point part is $z^N/N!$ times product Lebesgue measure, and let $\mu_{\mathcal R}$ have density $e^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{free}}}/\Xi_{\mathcal R}$ relative to $\Pi_{\mathcal R}$. By [L1] and Tonelli [F5],
$$E N_i^2=E N_i+E[N_i(N_i-1)] \leq \xi |C_i\cap\mathcal R|+\xi^2|C_i\cap\mathcal R|^2 \leq M:=\xi+\xi^2.$$
This gives a uniform second-moment bound for every unit cell in every such region. [F1, F3, F5, L1, algebra]

2.1 For each $\Omega_k$, let $\mathcal R_k$ be the union of unit cells meeting $\Omega_k$. Then $\Xi_{\Omega_k}\leq\Xi_{\mathcal R_k}$ by domain monotonicity, and $|\mathcal R_k|/|\Omega_k|\to1$ by the van Hove boundary condition. Put $J_0=\lceil R_0+2\rceil$, where $R_0$ is the regular-tail cutoff in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and choose $M_0\geq\max\{2B,\psi(J_0-1)\}$. For $j\in\mathbb Z^d$, define $\kappa_j=M_0$ when $|j|_\infty<J_0$ and $\kappa_j=\psi(|j|_\infty-1)$ otherwise. If two particles occupy cells with offset $j$, their negative pair energy is bounded by $\kappa_j$: for near offsets, stability on a two-point configuration gives $\phi(x)\geq-2B$, and for far offsets the regularity envelope applies. Also $\sum_j\kappa_j<\infty$ by [F1]–[F2]. Partition the cells of $\mathcal R_k$ into boxes $B$ of $\ell$ unit cells per side and, for each occupied cell $i$, set $e_i=\sum_{j:\,B(j)\neq B(i)}\kappa_{i-j}$. The negative cross-box energy obeys $W^-\leq\sum_i e_iN_i^2$, by $N_iN_j\leq(N_i^2+N_j^2)/2$ and summation over ordered cross-box cell pairs. Step 1.1 gives $E W^-\leq M\sum_i e_i$, so Markov's inequality shows $W^-\leq2M\sum_i e_i$ with probability at least $1/2$ (with probability one if the sum vanishes). On this event $H_{\mathrm{total}}\geq H_{\mathrm{in}}-2M\sum_i e_i$, where $H_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the sum of within-box energies. Therefore
$$\Xi_{\mathcal R_k}/2\leq e^{2\beta M\sum_i e_i}\prod_B\Xi_{\mathcal R_k\cap B}.$$
Indeed, $\Xi_{\mathcal R_k}\mu_{\mathcal R_k}(E)=\int_Ee^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{total}}}d\Pi_{\mathcal R_k}$; bound this by $e^{2\beta M\sum_i e_i}\int_Ee^{-\beta H_{\mathrm{in}}}d\Pi_{\mathcal R_k}$, then factor the latter integral by boxes. Each unrestricted partial-box partition is at most the full $\ell$-cube partition. For one full box, put $E_\ell=\sum_{i\in B,j\notin B}\kappa_{i-j}$. For fixed $R$, cells within distance $R$ of the boundary contribute at most $O_R(\ell^{d-1})\sum_j\kappa_j$, while every other cell contributes at most $\ell^d\sum_{|j|_\infty>R}\kappa_j$. Thus $E_\ell/\ell^d\to0$, by first letting $\ell\to\infty$ and then $R\to\infty$. Consequently
$$\limsup_k|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k} \leq\ell^{-d}\bigl[\log\Xi_{\Lambda_\ell}+2\beta M E_\ell\bigr].$$
Let $\ell\to\infty$ and use [F4]. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, L1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For the lower bound, put $q=ze^{\beta B}$ and choose $K>eq+1$. Each core has at most $(K+1)\ell^d$ particles. If two tile indices differ by maximum norm $m\geq1$, their core points are separated by at least $mg$; hence the positive cross energy per core is at most
$$C_d(K+1)^2\ell^{2d}\sum_{m\geq1}m^{d-1}\psi(mg)\leq C'_d(K+1)^2\ell^{2d}g^{-d}\eta(g).$$
Summing over cores, using the exact ordered-label assignment count to cancel the global $N!$, and discarding negative cross energy gives
$$\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)\geq e^{-\beta D_{k,\ell,g}}(\Xi_\ell^{\rm cut})^{M_k},\qquad \frac{D_{k,\ell,g}}{|\Omega_k|}\leq C'_d(K+1)^2\left(\frac{\ell}{g}\right)^d\eta(g)+o_k(1).$$
First let $k\to\infty$.
